title: Pistachio Gelato with Steeped Pistachio Milk
summary: Ground pistachios steeped in hot milk, strained and cooked into a light custard with a little cornflour, then churned into dense, nutty gelato.
equipment: sieve lined with a triple layer of muslin

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Grind the nuts
steps.text: Process the pistachios in the food processor for about 20 seconds until finely ground.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Heat the 840 ml milk, cream, 110 g sugar, corn syrup and salt in the large saucepan until tiny bubbles form at the edge. Take off the heat, stir in the pistachios, cover and leave for 1 h to infuse.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour the mixture through the muslin-lined sieve into a bowl. Gather up the cloth and squeeze firmly to extract as much pistachio milk as possible. Discard the pulp.

steps.title: Mix the yolks
steps.text: In the second bowl whisk the yolks, 40 g sugar, cornflour and 60 ml milk until smooth.

steps.title: Cook the custard
steps.text: Rewarm the pistachio milk in the rinsed pan until steaming. Whisk a ladleful into the yolk mixture, then pour it all into the pan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring and scraping the base, for 4-6 min until thickened and at 85 °C.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Pour into a clean bowl and let it stop steaming, about 20 min. Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 h, until thoroughly cold.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Whisk the custard, then churn for 15-30 min until it is thick like soft serve.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the container, pressing out air pockets, cover the surface and freeze for about 6 h. Gelato is best served softer than ice cream: move it to the fridge 30-60 min before scooping.

tips: Peeled Sicilian or Iranian pistachios give the greenest colour and deepest flavour.
Squeeze the muslin hard: most of the flavour is in the last of the milk.
The cornflour keeps the gelato smooth without extra cream.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep frozen and covered for up to 5 days; soften in the fridge before serving.
